one_month_reasoning: In the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 29 before the open (consensus Q3 EPS $1.37), with the five-year capital and financing roll-forward (2027-31) and normally 2027 guidance (consensus FY2027 $4.54; my build $4.40). Also: the MN gas rate decision (Nov 2026) and the Minneapolis moratorium review (by Nov 21, just after the window). The Anthropic IPO most likely falls after the window: Polymarket gave 54% to a listing by Nov 30 and 74% by Dec 15 (CoinGape, Sep 22, $3.68M traded across the date contracts), so any IPO-funding flow mostly lands after Nov 19. What I expect from Oct 29: a bigger capital plan is likely, with a 2027 guide midpoint near or slightly below consensus because of the MN freeze proposal and Colorado's historical test year; the equity mix of the increment is the swing factor. The 10y has eased from 5.31% (Oct 5) to 5.12%, which supported the bounce off the $68.72 low. Net: a small positive drift (median ~$76.9) with event-widened monthly vol of ~5.8% (normal 19%/3.5 = 5.4%), close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of a P/E leg on a rate-base EPS build (NTM EPS at the horizon $4.70 x 17.3x less $0.23 Smokehouse = $81.08, weight 0.8) and a driver FCFF DCF (WACC 6.55%, g 3.5%, net debt $48.5B, 658M shares: $50.80, weight 0.2 from the 16.9x forward-P/E band). Engine base horizon value $75.03 (ex-dividend; ~$2.4/sh of dividends over the year comes on top).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-10-20 $4.70 (0.2 x FY2027 $4.40 + 0.8 x FY2028 $4.77 from the rate-base build on 652M/683M avg shares) x 17.3x (12-peer NTM median 18.85x, 0.92x relative), less $150M Smokehouse adjustment / 658M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Company base-plan rate base from the Q2 2026 presentation ($60B plan, ~11% CAGR). I add about half of the $10B+ line-of-sight capital (generation for ~3 GW incremental data-centre demand) in 2029-30: +$2B 2029, +$4B 2030 vs the base plan's $90B/$94B; each $1B adds ~20-25bp of RB growth per the deck.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Base plan only (no incremental) lowers 2030 EPS by ~3% (~-$1.5/share at 17.5x); full $10B+ adds ~+3%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Calibrated so that 2026 avg RB $61B x 53% equity x 8.75% = $2.83B less holdco/other drag $0.28B = $2.55B = guidance midpoint $4.10 x 622M shares. TTM ongoing ROEs: NSPM 9.59%, NSPW 10.31%, PSCo 7.22%, SPS 8.51%, total opco 8.43% (deck). Round 2: 2028 raised from 8.7% to 8.75% because the NSPM 2027-28 freeze filing offsets lost base-rate increases with accelerated ITCs (8-K, no EPS effect stated by the company), so I no longer take an extra 5bp off for it; PSCo's 13-month historical test year (CPUC, $157M of $356M) keeps the consolidated figure flat rather than rising.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the MN freeze is approved without the full ITC offset and CO keeps historical test years, earned ROE -30bp, EPS -3.5% (~-$2.8/share): the bear case.

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q forward schedule: 2025 forwards 12.2M + 15.1M settle Dec-2026 to May-2027; 2026 forwards 21.2M + 21.3M mature Dec-2027 to Dec-2028 (Xcel may settle any time before). DRIP/benefit plans issued $64M in H1 2026 (~1.7M shares/yr at ~$76). FY2027 = 624.6 + DRIP 1.5 + 27.3 x ~0.85 outstanding share of the year (23.2) + treasury-method dilution on unsettled 2026 forwards ~2 + plan shares ~0.5 = ~652M. FY2028 = 624.6 + 27.3 + DRIP 3.2 + half of the 42.5M 2026 forwards on average (21.3) + ~1 treasury + ATM for part of the ~$1.05B uncontracted equity (~$0.4B / $76 = 5.3) = ~683M. 2029-30: all 69.8M forwards settled plus DRIP and the rest of the ATM. Round 1's 645M/664M missed the 2026 forwards' timing.

NI / avg diluted shares: 2,866/652 = $4.40; 3,260/683 = $4.77; 3,580/703 = $5.09; 3,810/712 = $5.35. FY2027 $4.40 is 3.1% below consensus $4.54 (19 analysts); FY2028 $4.77 is 2.1% below a 9% path off the $4.10 guide midpoint ($4.47, $4.87). The gap is CO/MN lag and the 2026 forwards landing in FY2028 shares.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Consensus/guide path (FY2027 $4.54, FY2028 ~$4.87) would lift NTM EPS at the horizon ~2.5% to ~$4.81 (+$2.0/share on the P/E leg).

inputs_detail.derivation: 12-peer median NTM P/E 18.85x (range 13.7x ES to 21.5x ETR). XEL today ~17.2x NTM ($76.68 / $4.46 = 0.2 x 4.12 + 0.8 x 4.54), i.e. 0.91x relative. 17.3x = 0.92x relative: a slightly wider discount than round 1's 17.5x because only ~$80M of Smokehouse insurance is left (not $525M of cover as I wrote), Moody's outlooks are negative and PSCo earns 7.2%; offset by ~9% EPS growth vs the ~8% peer median, so not widened further. NTM EPS at 2027-10-20 = 0.2 x $4.40 + 0.8 x $4.77 = $4.70. Gate note: consistent-basis peer median 18.45x (supervisor re-weighting of peers.json to XEL's Oct-2026 window 0.197 FY2026 / 0.803 FY2027; the peers.md table median 18.85x mixes NTM windows: WEC, CMS, AEE, ES use 0.504/0.496 and LNT, PPL, CNP, EVRG 0.753/0.247); on it XEL today is 0.93x and this 17.3x is 0.94x. Holding 0.92x on the consistent median would be 17.0x (-$1.5/sh on the P/E leg); the agent's chosen 17.3x is kept as its view.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At the peer median 18.85x the leg is $88.4; at 15x (bear, 10y >= 5.5%) $70.3.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 release: $460M estimated losses ($503M with legal costs), $404M settled, $56M remaining probable losses, and only ~$80M of the $525M policy left (round 1 wrongly treated $525M as available cover). Headroom over the remaining accrual is ~$24M, so further claims and any Texas AG penalty (not estimable; the suit also seeks to bar cost recovery) are largely uninsured. inputs_detail.variant_view: A Texas AG outcome >$1B with recovery barred would be ~-$1.2/share after tax (bear).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF FY2026-30 from revenue +6.5%/+9%/+8.5%/+6.5%/+5.5%, EBIT (pretax+interest) 26.4%->31.1%, tax 0%, D&A ~20-21%, capex 80%->51% then 37.5% normalised; WACC 6.55% (10y 5.12%); Gordon g 3.5%; net debt at horizon $48.5B; 658M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: us-gaap:RegulatedAndUnregulatedOperatingRevenue FY2025 from the 10-K XBRL (the fact pack lacks a revenue tag; read from data.sec.gov companyfacts, accession 0000072903-26-000009).

Non-fuel revenue requirement tracks rate base (~11% CAGR), fuel/purchased power (~35-40% of revenue) is pass-through and flat; FY2026 $15,622M vs consensus $15,606M; FY2027 $17,028M vs consensus $17,150M (-0.7%). Consensus from the Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES snapshot (retrieved 2026-10-20T21:17:18Z): $15,606M / $17,150M. 14,669 x 1.065 = 15,622; x 1.09 = 17,028.

EBIT_t = pretax_t + interest_t, with pretax = NI/1.10 (TTM tax is a net benefit: -$231M on $2,002M pretax, F74/F81) and interest $1.80B, $2.10B, $2.45B, $2.75B, $3.00B (TTM $1,642M, F67, growing with debt). 2026: 2,318+1,800 = 4,118 / 15,622 = 26.4%; 2030: 3,464+3,000 = 6,464 / 20,758 = 31.1%. Not GAAP operating income (F6 $2,789M TTM) because AFUDC-equity and other income are part of regulated earnings. FY2028: 3,260/1.10 + 2,450 = 5,414 / 18,475 = 29.3%. The TTM tax benefit (-11.5%) would imply NI/1.115 rather than /1.10; immaterial (~$0.03B of EBIT).
Reported income tax has been a net benefit three years running (-$146M, -$402M, -$245M; TTM -$231M) as PTC/ITC transfers exceed tax; 0% is a conservative proxy for cash taxes over the plan.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At a 10% tax rate the DCF falls ~$7/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Capex = change in rate base + D&A: 2026 ~$12.5B (TTM $12,463M, F53) / 15,622 = 80.0%; 2027 $11.0B + $3.4B = $14.4B / 17,029 = 84.6%; 2028 $9.0B + $3.75B = $12.75B / 18,476 = 69.0%; 2029 $6.0B + $4.05B = $10.05B / 19,677 = 51.0%. FY2030 steady state for the Gordon terminal: D&A $4.35B + 3.5% x $98B = $7.78B / 20,759 = 37.5%, not the plan's ~$10B. The earlier '$14.2B' and '$12.6B' sums did not compute; the model rows still carry 83.4% / 68.2% ($0.2B / $0.15B less capex).
inputs_detail.variant_view: On the corrected 84.6% / 69.0% rows the agent's DCF is $50.53 (-$0.27) and its blend $74.97 (-$0.06): engine re-run in the gate fix, not adopted (agent view).

inputs_detail.derivation: Cost of equity 8.42% = 10y UST 5.12% on 2026-10-20 (Treasury par curve; round 1 used the 4.9% Sep average, now corrected) + beta 0.6 x ERP 5.5%; pre-tax debt 5.4% (blend of embedded and 2026 issues 4.15%-5.875%) x (1-21%) = 4.27%; market weights E $47.9B (624.6M x $76.68) / D $39.5B = 55/45: 0.55 x 8.42% + 0.45 x 4.27% = 6.55%. Polymarket priced 96.8% for no Fed cut in 2026.
inputs_detail.variant_view: An implied ERP of ~4.5% instead of 5.5% gives CoE 7.8% and WACC ~6.2%, lifting the DCF leg to roughly $58 (+$1.5/share on the blend).

inputs_detail.derivation: Rate-base growth continues after 2030 at ~3.5% (replacement capex, load growth from data centres and electrification) but well below the 11% plan CAGR; held at 3.5% rather than 4% for the stranded-cost tail when 15-year large-load contracts end in the 2040s (see long_dated_risks).

Jul-2026 to Oct-2027: capex H2-2026 $7.82B + 0.8 x 2027 $15.13B = $19.92B (deck capex by year, front-loaded: 2026-27 = $28.9B of $60B); less CFO net of dividends ~$5.9B; less 2025 forward minimum proceeds $932M + $1,044M = $1.98B: $37.45B + 19.92 - 5.9 - 1.98 = $49.5B; less ~$1.0B of tax-credit-transfer and DRIP cash above the TTM run-rate (judgment) = ~$48.5B. Round 1 ($48.3B) used lower H2-26/2027 capex ($6.5B/$14.2B).

624.6M (cover, 2026-07-28) + 27.3M 2025 forwards (settle by May-2027) + DRIP ~2.2M (1.25 yr x 1.7M) + treasury-method dilution on unsettled 2026 forwards ~2M + ATM ~2M = ~658M. Above the 651.9M floor; below the supervisor's 662M because I assume the uncontracted equity is back-end weighted.

bear.story: 10y holds >=5.3% (group P/E -1.5 to -2 turns), CO/MN lag deepens (earned ROE -30bp: MN freeze approved without full ITC offset, CO keeps historical test years), Texas AG Smokehouse outcome beyond the ~$80M insurance left, ESAs slip under organised opposition; ~14.8x on ~$4.51. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.3x NTM, 0.92x the 18.85x median and inside the range; XEL trades at ~17.2x today ($76.68 / NTM $4.46), 0.91x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is one I expect to last through the horizon, for reasons in the filings and rate orders: (1) wildfire liability is open: Smokehouse Creek has $460M of estimated losses, $56M still probable, only ~$80M of the $525M policy left, a pending Texas AG suit and no Colorado liability statute; (2) PSCo, 43% of rate base, earns 7.22% against an allowed 9.3%, and the CPUC granted $157M of $356M on a 13-month historical test year; (3) Minnesota proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze; (4) Moody's outlooks are negative. Against that, XEL's ~9% EPS growth beats the ~8% peer median, so I hold the current relative (0.91-0.92x) rather than widen it toward ES's 13.7x. A move to the median needs a Colorado wildfire statute or a cleaner CO/MN outcome: the bull case.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$64 (13.6x my NTM EPS $4.70, ~7% under the $68.72 52-week low that XEL hit with the 10y at its 5.31% peak in early October) rates alone are unlikely to be the cause, so the market would be pricing a fundamental break: a new at-fault wildfire or a Texas AG outcome with losses beyond the ~$80M of Smokehouse insurance left and cost recovery barred, a regulatory reset (MN freeze without offset, CO ROE cuts), a downgrade that forces block equity, or guidance with EPS growth below ~6%. Re-underwrite there rather than average down. I keep $64 (supervisor $63): my EPS is ~2% lower, so the same multiple floor sits at a similar price.

Any de-risking sale of AI-linked utilities is a flow effect, not an earnings change

reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 17.3x P/E leg implies a 6.0% WACC against my 6.55%. With after-tax debt at 4.27% and 45% weight, that is a cost of equity of ~7.4%, i.e. an ERP of ~3.8% over the 5.12% 10y, about 1pt under my CAPM figure. Put another way, the multiple assumes EPS growth of ~8-9% to 2030 (rate base ~11% less ~3% dilution and lag) and then ~3.5% for good, an earned ROE that stays above the cost of equity (allowed 9.3-9.6%), and no permanent wildfire impairment. Plausible: 2 GW of signed or under-construction data-centre load on 15-year terms and the post-2030 pipeline back the growth. The long-dated risks (about -$2.6/share probability-weighted net of the Colorado upside) are why I use 17.3x rather than the 18.85x median.

sbc_treatment.note: SBC $46M FY2025 (F36), 0.3% of revenue, is expensed in GAAP and ongoing EPS; no add-back, so the share count carries only equity-plan issuance (forwards, DRIP, ATM), not SBC dilution. Peers' consensus is on the same operating-EPS basis.

reasoning: Round 2. Start: $76.68, -5.5% over a year, after wildfire litigation (Smokehouse Creek, Texas AG), MN/CO regulatory pressure (CPUC $157M of $356M on a historical test year; NSPM 2027-28 freeze filing) and a 10y that peaked at 5.31% on Oct 5 and closed at 5.12% on Oct 20. Supervisor fixes I accept: (1) the 10y is 5.12%, not 4.9%: CoE 8.42%, WACC 6.55%, DCF leg falls from $59.2 to $50.8; (2) only ~$80M of Smokehouse insurance remains: I keep -$150M (more than the supervisor's -$80M because the cover is nearly gone) and narrow my P/E from 17.5x to 17.3x; (3) shares: the 2025 forwards (27.3M) settle by May-2027 and the 2026 forwards (42.5M) from Dec-2027 to Dec-2028, so horizon shares are 658M (floor 651.9M plus DRIP, treasury dilution and a little ATM) and FY2028 average shares 683M; my round-1 path (645M/664M) missed this, which cuts FY2028 EPS from $4.88 to $4.77 after I lift 2028 earned ROE to 8.75% (the freeze is ITC-offset). I do not keep the supervisor's suggestion to hold $4.88: the corrected share count has to flow through. NTM EPS at the horizon $4.70 (supervisor $4.79; consensus-equivalent ~$4.87); (4) net debt at the horizon $48.5B from front-loaded capex; (5) the Abernathy-Anthropic link is dropped: the TeraWulf 8-K names Fluidstack with a Google backstop and pass-through power. Valuation: 17.3x x $4.70 - $0.23 = $81.1 (weight 0.8) and DCF $50.8 (0.2) = $75.03, 2% under spot, plus a ~3% dividend: fairly priced to slightly rich. Alternative-lane signals: organised data-centre opposition (Data Center Watch; MN AG on Pine Island; metro moratoria) is a real approval risk that Anthropic's S-1 risk factor confirms; Polymarket prices no 2026 Fed cut; prediction markets put the Anthropic IPO mostly in late Nov-Dec 2026. Kilian's liquidity-drain question: Tunguz estimates $432-576B of liquidity for the three mega-IPOs at normal floats, but expected 3-8% floats mean the actual raise is far smaller (reports say up to $100B for Anthropic) and S&P 500 inclusion is delayed; index funds would fund it by selling mega-cap tech, not utilities. XEL's holders (income and utility funds) overlap little with IPO buyers, and the S-1 does not change XEL's earnings; the only channel is the AI-power trade (XEL partly trades as a data-centre load name). So I expect at most a short, flow-driven dip. Plan: if XEL drops to ~$70-72 on IPO flow or rates with the Oct-29 plan intact (no extra equity beyond ~40% of incremental capex, 2027 guide >= ~$4.40), that is a buying opportunity: $70 is 14.9x NTM $4.70, ~7% under my value plus ~3% dividend (~10% 12-month total return). Do not buy a dip that comes with a wildfire or regulatory headline; below $64 is the thesis break: re-underwrite. Ladder: lognormal mixture around the engine scenarios ($59.7/$75.0/$88.3 at 25/50/25, 12% within-scenario vol, 4% weight on a 35%-vol tail), shifted half-way to spot because the price itself beats fair-value blends as a 12-month forecast; median ~$75.6, P(>=77) 0.46. Research: 9 web queries this round; Reddit/X gave nothing usable; no current Polymarket volume for the 2027-deadline Anthropic market was found. Lane: 18 of 32 sources are alternative; the rest are filings, data and the brief's WSJ fact, which the brief allows for basic facts.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility. The value is carried by a P/E leg (weight 0.8) on a rate-base EPS build: average rate base x 53% equity ratio x earned ROE (8.75-8.8%) less holdco interest, divided by a share count that follows the 10-Q forward-equity schedule (652M FY2027, 683M FY2028 avg). A driver FCFF DCF (weight 0.2, from the forward P/E band: $76.68 / FY2027 consensus $4.54 = 16.9x, so 15.0-19.6x gives 0.2) values the regulated asset base; EBIT is pretax + interest (includes AFUDC-equity) so NOPAT matches the earnings build. No segment build: the 10-K does not give revenue by opco in XBRL, and the opco split enters through the earned-ROE calibration (NSPM 35%, PSCo 43%, SPS 16%, NSPW 6% of 2025 rate base).
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value (75.03).

model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $50.8 vs P/E leg $81.1 (-37%). The FCFF DCF values the regulated asset base at a 6.55% WACC (CoE 8.42% on the 5.12% 10y): EV at the horizon ~1.0-1.1x rate base, because the after-tax regulated return (~6.5-6.8%) is about equal to the WACC and the 2026-28 capex wave earns its return only with lag. The market prices XEL and peers at ~1.3x EV/rate base: the engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg implies a 6.0% WACC, i.e. a cost of equity ~7.4% with the same debt cost, or an ERP of ~3.8% over a 5.12% 10y. The gap is the value of allowed ROEs (9.3-9.6%) above a ~7.5% market cost of equity, which my CAPM CoE does not credit. Kept at the 0.2 weight from the forward-P/E band, not zeroed: it is the asset-value anchor and the downside if utility multiples de-rate toward book-plus-growth.
